mainTopic: Redeeming dead קדשים and the rules of העמדה והערכה according to רבי שמעון, the רבנן, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, followed by a new משנה listing items that are buried and items that are burned.
overview: The גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that we may redeem קדשים just to feed them to dogs. The proof is rejected because the animals in that ברייתא were slaughtered, so their meat is fit for people. רבי זירא then explains why, according to רבי שמעון, unblemished בדק הבית animals are buried: they are fit for the מזבח, and anything fit for the מזבח never leaves it. Next, רב פפא (or רבא) challenges רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees a בעל מום מעיקרו is not included in העמדה והערכה. The challenge comes from רב's comment on a משנה in בכורות. אביי answers that the 'חכמים' רב quoted are a תנא from the school of לוי. The גמרא then explains רב's wording in two ways: either he follows ריש לקיש, or he follows רבי יוחנן and meant 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.' Finally, a new משנה lists the forbidden items that must be buried and those that must be burned.

steps.title: Attempted proof that we redeem sacred animals to feed dogs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says blemished animals that died are redeemed. We explained it as a case where the consecration came before the blemish. So it seems we may redeem קדשים even when the only use left is feeding them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: 'Blemished animals shall be redeemed.' We explained that this is a case where they were consecrated before they got the blemish. So learn from it: we may redeem sacred animals in order to feed them to dogs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and draws a proof from it. Dead animals are redeemed, and a dead animal is only good for dogs, so it seems we redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals were consecrated while unblemished, so they had real holiness on their body. Even so, the ברייתא says to redeem them after they died. Since a dead animal (נבלה) can only go to dogs, this looks like proof that redemption is allowed just for dog food.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemished animals, which cannot be offered on the מזבח
They shall be redeemed, meaning their holiness moves onto money
We set up the case as, meaning we explained which situation the source is talking about
Their consecration came before their blemish
We redeem sacred animals to feed them to dogs. This is the question being debated.

phrases.english: blemished ones shall be redeemed;
and we established it
as a case where their consecration preceded their blemish;
learn from it
that we redeem sacred animals to feed them to dogs!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section and draws a conclusion from the ברייתא quoted there.
steps.raayaObject: That one may redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying blemished animals that died are redeemed, explained as a case where consecration came before the blemish.

steps.title: Rejection: the animals were slaughtered, not dead on their own
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. The ברייתא is talking about animals that someone slaughtered against the rules, so their meat is still fit for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where someone went against the rule and slaughtered them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It explains that the animals in the ברייתא were not dead on their own; someone slaughtered them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished sacred animal should be redeemed before it is slaughtered. Here someone slaughtered it first, which is wrong. But because it was properly slaughtered, the meat is kosher for people, so the redemption is for human food and not for dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This phrase sets up a narrower reading of a source.
He went against the rule and slaughtered them, meaning before redeeming them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא changed its wording. The גמרא is only saying that 'died' here means 'slaughtered,' not a natural death.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
Where he transgressed and slaughtered them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The ברייתא says nothing about redeeming for dogs.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the animals died naturally and became נבלה. Really they were slaughtered, so the meat is fit for people.

steps.title: Supporting ברייתא: slaughtered blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that this case, a blemished sacred animal slaughtered before redemption, is a known case. רבי מאיר says bury it, and חכמים say redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: all sacred animals that got a blemish and someone slaughtered them, רבי מאיר says they must be buried, and חכמים say they can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that redeeming an animal slaughtered before redemption is a real, discussed case. This supports the rejection in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is exactly the one the גמרא just described: blemished קדשים slaughtered before redemption. חכמים allow redeeming them even after slaughter. That fits the ברייתא from step 1 without any proof about feeding dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish fell on them, meaning they became blemished
They must be buried and cannot be used at all
The Sages, the majority view that disagrees with an individual

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about redeeming dead blemished animals means slaughtered ones. Their meat is for people, so it proves nothing about redeeming for dogs.

phrases.english: As it is taught: all sacred animals
that developed a blemish, and he slaughtered them,
Rabbi Meir says: they shall be buried;
and the Rabbis say: they shall be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source showing that the case described in step 2 is a recognized case.
steps.raayaObject: That redeeming blemished קדשים slaughtered before redemption is a real case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר (bury them) and חכמים (redeem them).

steps.title: Why are unblemished animals buried according to רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: רבי שמעון says קדשי בדק הבית were not included in העמדה והערכה. If so, why does he say unblemished ones must be buried?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: according to רבי שמעון, who said that animals consecrated for the upkeep of the Temple were not included in 'standing and valuation,' why must unblemished ones be buried?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי ירמיה points out what looks like a contradiction inside רבי שמעון's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קדשי בדק הבית are not under העמדה והערכה, they can be redeemed even after death. Yet the earlier ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון says unblemished ones that died must be buried. Why does being unblemished change the rule?

keyTerms.meaning: Things consecrated for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח
Standing and valuation: the animal must stand alive before a כהן to be valued, so a dead one cannot be redeemed
Unblemished animals
Why?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
According to Rabbi Shimon, who said:
things consecrated for Temple maintenance
were not included in standing and valuation,
why shall unblemished ones be buried?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא quoted before step 1, where רבי שמעון said unblemished animals that died are buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of questioning about רבי שמעון's view in the ברייתא behind step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why unblemished בדק הבית animals that died are buried according to רבי שמעון, when he holds בדק הבית is not under העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: Because they are fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that unblemished animals are fit to be offered on the מזבח, so they are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are fit for sacrifice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. Unblemished animals are buried because they are fit to be brought as קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though they were given to בדק הבית, an unblemished animal could have gone on the מזבח. Because of that fitness, it is treated like altar holiness, which falls under העמדה והערכה. So once it dies it cannot be redeemed and must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: They are fit or suitable
Offering on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, בדק הבית animals are normally redeemable even after death. Unblemished ones are the exception, because they are fit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Because they are fit for sacrifice.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזוּ לְהַקְרָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unblemished animals are fit for the מזבח, so they get the stricter treatment and are buried rather than redeemed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the answer: anything fit for the altar stays with the altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up רבי זירא's answer. Unblemished animals given to בדק הבית can be redeemed only for the מזבח, because anything fit for the מזבח never leaves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone consecrates unblemished animals for Temple upkeep, they can be redeemed only for the altar. Anything that is fit for the altar never leaves the altar's hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי זירא's answer from step 5. The answer was that unblemished animals are treated differently because they are fit for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unblemished animal given to בדק הבית is still fit to be offered. So it is sold only to someone who will bring it as a קרבן. This shows that 'fit for the מזבח' gives the animal a special, stronger status. That explains why רבי שמעון says unblemished ones must be buried and not simply redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates something by linking it to something already holy
Temple upkeep fund (holy property that is not for the מזבח)
Unblemished animals, fit to be offered
It never leaves the altar's hold

steps.whatToRemember: Anything fit for the מזבח stays connected to the מזבח, even if it was given to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple upkeep,
when they are redeemed,
they are redeemed only for the altar,
phrases.notes: He means they are sold only to someone who will offer them as a קרבן.

phrases.english: for anything that is fit for the altar
never leaves the altar's hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a ברייתא supporting רבי זירא's answer
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that animals fit for the מזבח get special treatment
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: unblemished animals given to בדק הבית are redeemed only for the מזבח

steps.title: Is it true that everyone agrees about an animal blemished from the start?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רבא) asks אביי a question. רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees that a בעל מום מעיקרו was not included in העמדה והערכה. Is that really so?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי (some say it was רבא): According to רבי יוחנן, who explains the ברייתא as talking about an animal blemished from the start, everyone agrees that such an animal was not included in standing and valuation. But is that really true?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. It doubts רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees, and it sets up the challenge from a משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the ברייתא is about an animal whose blemish came before its consecration. He said both רבי שמעון and חכמים agree that such an animal does not need העמדה והערכה. The words 'וְלָא?!' question that 'everyone agrees' claim.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal blemished from the start, before it was consecrated
Standing and valuation: standing the animal before a כהן to set its value
Who explains it as (sets the case as)
Everyone (all opinions)

phrases.english: רב פפא said to אביי,
and some say it was רבא who said it:
According to רבי יוחנן, who explains it
as talking about an animal blemished from the start,
and everyone holds
that an animal blemished from the start
was not included in standing and valuation.
And it was not?!
phrases.notes: This is surprise: is it really true that everyone agrees?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי זירא's discussion back to רבי יוחנן's position and starts questioning it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do all opinions really agree that a בעל מום מעיקרו is not included in העמדה והערכה?

steps.title: A משנה about animals blemished before they were consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה listing the laws of animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration. It ends with 'if they died, they are redeemed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: All consecrated animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration, once redeemed, are subject to firstborn status and the priestly gifts. They become fully non-sacred, so they may be shorn and worked. Their offspring and milk are permitted after redemption. One who slaughters them outside is exempt. They do not make a substitute. And if they died, they are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for its challenge to רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees. How exactly this משנה pushes against him is spelled out in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats an animal blemished before consecration as having only weak holiness. Once redeemed it is completely ordinary, and slaughtering it outside brings no punishment. Its last line, 'if they died, they are redeemed,' is about the exact case רבי יוחנן was discussing. The גמרא will use that line to test whether everyone really agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish
Firstborn status (here, for the animal's future firstborn)
The priestly gifts: foreleg, jaw and maw
To be shorn and to be worked
One who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard
A substitute: an animal swapped for a holy one, which becomes holy too

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying these animals were never holy at all. Their holiness is weak, so their value goes to buy a proper קרבן, and they need redemption before ordinary use.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
phrases.english: All consecrated animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration
and were redeemed,
are subject to firstborn status and to the priestly gifts,
phrases.notes: Firstborn status here means their future firstborn babies will be a בכור.

phrases.english: and they go out to be fully non-sacred, to be shorn and to be worked.
Their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption,
one who slaughters them outside is exempt,
they do not make a substitute,
and if they died, they are redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the doubt raised in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees a בעל מום מעיקרו was not included in העמדה והערכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה (בכורות 14a) gives the laws for this exact category, ending 'if they died, they are redeemed.' The גמרא goes on to use it to test whether all opinions really agree.

steps.title: רב: The משנה Follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה about animals whose blemish came before consecration follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that קדשי מזבח were included in העמדה והערכה, but קדשי בדק הבית were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in רב's name: This משנה follows רבי שמעון. He said that animals given to the altar were included in 'standing and valuation,' but animals given to Temple upkeep were not. We learned this in a משנה: רבי שמעון says that Temple-upkeep animals that died are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's statement about who wrote the משנה from Step 8. This sets up the challenge to רבי יוחנן that comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ties the משנה to רבי שמעון's view. In that view, altar animals were included in העמדה והערכה, so if they die they must be buried. Temple-upkeep animals were not included, so they can be redeemed even after death.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Standing and valuation': the animal had to be stood before a כהן and valued in order to be redeemed. If it died first, it could not be redeemed.
Animals consecrated to be offered on the altar
Things consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, whose value goes to the Temple treasury
They can be redeemed (exchanged for money)

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the view of Rabbi Shimon,
who said that animals consecrated for the altar
were included in the law of standing and valuation,
but animals consecrated for Temple upkeep were not,
as we learned in a משנה:
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ.
phrases.english: Animals consecrated for Temple upkeep, if they died, are redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains whose opinion the משנה from Step 8 follows, which builds toward the challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי שמעון: altar animals were included in העמדה והערכה, and Temple-upkeep animals were not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון Agrees About an Animal Blemished From the Start
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees that a בעל מום מעיקרו given to the altar is redeemed if it dies. The word 'אותה' in the פסוק excludes it from העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון agrees that an animal blemished from the start is redeemed. Why? Because the verse says 'it.' The word 'it' comes to exclude an animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues and explains how the משנה can follow רבי שמעון. Even though רבי שמעון includes altar animals in העמדה והערכה, he makes an exception for a בעל מום מעיקרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke about animals whose blemish came before they were consecrated. רבי שמעון agrees these are redeemed even after death, because the extra word 'אותה' excludes them from the requirement of standing and valuation. So an altar animal remains in the category of קדשי מזבח, but this kind gets an exceptional outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that already had a permanent blemish before it was consecrated
Agrees (concedes on this point)
To exclude: a word in the פסוק comes to leave something out of the law

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon agrees
about an animal blemished from the start, that it is redeemed.
What is the reason?
Because the verse says: "it,"
and "it" comes to exclude an animal blemished from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁנִּפְדֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי שמעון's exception, which explains why the משנה says these animals are redeemed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a בעל מום מעיקרו is excluded from העמדה והערכה by the word 'אותה', so it is redeemed.

steps.title: But the Sages Include Even an Animal Blemished From the Start
steps.stepSummary: רב's statement ends by saying that the חכמים include even a בעל מום מעיקרו in העמדה והערכה. This contradicts רבי יוחנן, who said everyone agrees it was not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: even an animal blemished from the start was included in standing and valuation!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch of the challenge. רב's words show that there is a view, the חכמים, that does include a בעל מום מעיקרו, so not everyone agrees as רבי יוחנן claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, רבי יוחנן said that all opinions exclude a בעל מום מעיקרו. Here רב says the חכמים include it. If these חכמים are the ones who argue with רבי שמעון in the משנה, then רבי יוחנן's 'everyone agrees' is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Sages': the majority opinion that disagrees with a named sage
Even

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
even an animal blemished from the start
was included in the law of standing and valuation!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ הָיָה בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's statement and turns it into a direct challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (Step 7) that everyone agrees a בעל מום מעיקרו was not included in העמדה והערכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב quotes חכמים who do include a בעל מום מעיקרו, so the matter is disputed and not agreed by everyone.

steps.title: These חכמים Are a תנא From the School of לוי
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the 'חכמים' in רב's statement are not the רבנן of the משנה. They are a תנא from the school of לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who are these 'חכמים'? A תנא of the school of לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יוחנן. He says the 'חכמים' רב mentioned are a different, outside opinion, not the main רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's 'everyone agrees' was about רבי שמעון and the רבנן of the משנה. A separate תנא from the school of לוי may disagree, but that does not break רבי יוחנן's statement about the main dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (sage of the משנה period) from the study house of לוי, whose teachings were collected separately
Who?

phrases.english: He said to him: Who are 'the Sages'?
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רב פפא (or רבא) here.

phrases.english: A tanna of the school of Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן חֲכָמִים? תַּנָּא דְּבֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by identifying the 'חכמים' as someone else.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the speaker: the 'חכמים' are a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'חכמים' are the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון in the משנה, so רבי יוחנן is contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'חכמים' are a תנא from the school of לוי, so the רבנן of the משנה can still agree with רבי שמעון, as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: Then Rav Should Have Said the משנה Fits Both Sides
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן of the משנה also agree that a בעל מום מעיקרו is redeemed, why did רב say the משנה follows only רבי שמעון? He should have said it follows רבי שמעון and those who argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he said 'This is the view of רבי שמעון' and nothing more? He should have said 'This is the view of רבי שמעון and those who disagree with him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner pushes back on אביי's answer by looking closely at רב's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, both רבי שמעון and the רבנן of the משנה agree that a בעל מום מעיקרו is redeemed. If so, the משנה fits both opinions. Saying 'this is רבי שמעון's view' suggests that it fits only him.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more (only this)
His disputants: those who argue with him
He should have said it this way

phrases.english: If so,
"This is the view of Rabbi Shimon" and nothing more?
"This is the view of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him"
is what he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״ וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from Step 12 by pointing to רב's wording in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that the רבנן of the משנה agree with רבי שמעון about a בעל מום מעיקרו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both sides agree, the משנה fits both. רב should not have attributed it to רבי שמעון alone.

steps.title: רב Follows ריש לקיש's View of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רב did not credit the משנה to the רבנן because he holds like ריש לקיש. According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן hold that only קדשי בדק הבית were included in העמדה והערכה, and קדשי מזבח were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The reason he did not teach it that way is that רב holds like ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש said that according to the רבנן, Temple-upkeep animals were included in standing and valuation, and altar animals were not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why רב named only רבי שמעון. It comes from רב's understanding of what the רבנן hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן never include altar animals in העמדה והערכה at all, so for them a dead altar animal is always redeemed. The משנה's סיפא rules that animals whose consecration came before their blemish are buried if they died. That ruling cannot fit the רבנן, so רב named only רבי שמעון (the next step spells this out).

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like (agrees with the view of)
According to the רבנן (the majority view)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule survives. The 'חכמים' who include a בעל מום מעיקרו are a תנא from the school of לוי. רב credits the משנה to רבי שמעון alone because he follows ריש לקיש, who holds that for the רבנן, altar animals were never included in העמדה והערכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice that רבי שמעון and the רבנן (as ריש לקיש explains them) hold opposite views. רבי שמעון includes altar animals and excludes Temple-upkeep animals. The רבנן include Temple-upkeep animals and exclude altar animals.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The reason he did not teach it this way

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: is because Rav holds like Reish Lakish,
who said that according to the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: animals consecrated for Temple upkeep were included in standing and valuation,
but animals consecrated for the altar were not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַאי דְּלָא קָתָנֵי הָכִי, מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording by pointing to רב's view of the רבנן's position (following ריש לקיש).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both sides agree about a בעל מום מעיקרו, רב should have said the משנה fits both.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן exclude all altar animals from העמדה והערכה, so they would redeem even the סיפא's animals. The סיפא's ruling of burial therefore fits רבי שמעון alone.

steps.title: Why the last clause does not fit the רבנן according to ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: Continuing אביי's answer: the רישא (redeemed if they died) fits the רבנן, but the סיפא (buried if they died) does not fit them according to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part of the משנה says that if they died they are redeemed, but the last part says that if they died they are buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer by showing exactly which part of the משנה clashes with the רבנן according to ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן hold that קדשי מזבח were never included in העמדה והערכה, so they would always be redeemed after death. The רישא, 'if they died they are redeemed,' fits that view. The סיפא, 'if they died they are buried,' does not, so רב could not say the whole משנה follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
They are redeemed (exchanged for money)
They must be buried

phrases.english: And the first clause teaches: 'And if they died, they are redeemed,'
phrases.notes: This is the case of an animal that already had a blemish before it was given to the altar.

phrases.english: and the last clause teaches: 'If they died, they are buried.'
phrases.notes: According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן would redeem this animal too, so this clause can't be theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישָׁא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 14 by pointing to the סיפא as the clause that clashes with the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that part of the source contradicts one of the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן agree with the whole משנה, so רב should have mentioned them.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to ריש לקיש the סיפא's ruling of burial does not fit the רבנן, so רב correctly gave the משנה only to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Second answer: רב holds like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, רב holds like רבי יוחנן, and indeed his statement should read 'this follows רבי שמעון and those who argue with him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say that רב holds like רבי יוחנן. And as for what bothered you, that he should have said 'this is the opinion of רבי שמעון and his disputants,' say: yes, that is what he meant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer the question from step 13: it simply accepts the question's suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the רבנן agree that a בעל מום מעיקרו is redeemed, and they also agree that the סיפא's animals are buried. So the whole משנה fits both sides. Then we read רב's statement as 'this follows רבי שמעון and those who argue with him.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another answer
He holds (this opinion)
And those who argue with him
Indeed, that is so

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not reject אביי's first answer. It is a second, independent way out: instead of explaining why רב left out the רבנן, it says he really did include them.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
רב holds like רבי יוחנן,
and as for what was difficult for you,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the question in step 13.

phrases.aramaic: ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that he should have said 'this is the opinion of רבי שמעון and those who disagree with him,'
say: indeed, so he said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, רַב כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in step 13, instead of the ריש לקיש answer given in steps 14-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the question and adjusting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's statement credits the משנה only to רבי שמעון, so he must have excluded the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds like רבי יוחנן, and his statement should be understood as 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.'
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why רב mentioned only רבי שמעון. First: he holds like ריש לקיש, so the סיפא does not fit the רבנן. Second: he holds like רבי יוחנן, and he really meant 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.'

steps.title: New משנה: the list of items that must be buried
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists items that must be buried: miscarried sacrificial fetuses and placentas, the stoned ox, the עגלה ערופה, the birds of the מצורע, the hair of the נזיר, the פטר חמור, meat cooked in milk, and חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the things that are buried: sacrificial animals that miscarried, the fetus is buried; if one miscarried a placenta, it is buried; and the ox that is stoned, and the heifer whose neck is broken, and the birds of a מצורע, and the hair of a נזיר, and the firstborn donkey, and meat in milk, and non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a list of things that may not be used and must be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous part of the פרק dealt with whether dead קדשים are redeemed or buried. This משנה gathers items that must be buried, so that no one can benefit from them. The last item on the list, חולין slaughtered in the עזרה, sets up the disagreement with רבי שמעון in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The things that are buried
Placenta (afterbirth)
An ox stoned for killing a person
The heifer whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder
A firstborn donkey
Non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the things that are buried:
sacrificial animals that miscarried — the fetuses shall be buried,
if it miscarried a placenta — it shall be buried,
and an ox that is stoned, and a heifer whose neck is broken,
and the birds of a מצורע, and the hair of a נזיר,
and the firstborn of a donkey, and meat cooked in milk,
and non-holy animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּקְבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These listed items may not be used, and they must be buried.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and says חולין slaughtered in the עזרה must be burned, and the same applies to a wild animal slaughtered there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard are burned, and so too a wild animal slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the last item on the list. He says it should be burned, not buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא puts חולין שנשחטו בעזרה among the things that are buried. רבי שמעון says they are burned instead. He adds that even a חיה, a wild animal, slaughtered in the עזרה is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be burned
A wild (undomesticated) animal, like a deer
The Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not disagree with the rest of the list. He argues only about animals slaughtered in the עזרה.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
non-holy animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard shall be burned,
and likewise a wild animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
phrases.notes: A חיה is never brought as a קרבן, yet he still says it is burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה יִשָּׂרֵפוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the last item in the list of buried things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין and even a חיה slaughtered in the עזרה are burned, not buried.

steps.title: The list of items that must be burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the items that are burned: חמץ on פסח, impure תרומה, ערלה and כלאי הכרם. For the last two, whatever is normally burned is burned, and whatever is normally buried is buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the things that are burned: חמץ on פסח is burned, and so is impure תרומה. With ערלה and כלאי הכרם, things that are normally burned are burned, and things that are normally buried are buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the 'buried' list to a new list of things that must be burned instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning gets rid of the forbidden item completely, while burial only puts it out of reach. For ערלה and כלאי הכרם, the משנה does not give one rule for everything. The method depends on the type of item: solid foods get burned, and liquids, which cannot really be burned, get buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that must be destroyed by burning
Leavened food on פסח, which is forbidden
תרומה (the כהן's portion) that has become ritually impure and may not be eaten
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
Crops forbidden because they were planted mixed together in a vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'whose way is to be burned/buried' applies to ערלה and כלאי הכרם. It does not change the rule for חמץ or impure תרומה, which are simply burned.

phrases.english: And these are the items that are burned:
Leavened bread on Passover shall be burned,
and impure teruma,
and orla, and diverse kinds sown in a vineyard:
those whose manner is to be burned shall be burned,
phrases.notes: This means foods. They can be burned, so they are burned.

phrases.english: and those whose manner is to be buried shall be buried,
phrases.notes: This means liquids, like wine or oil. They can't really be burned, so they are buried instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּשְׂרָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the list of buried items (Step 17) with a second list of burned items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ on פסח and impure תרומה are burned. For ערלה and כלאי הכרם, foods are burned and liquids are buried.

steps.title: Lighting a fire with impure תרומה bread and oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that a person may light a fire using bread and oil of impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may light a fire with bread and oil of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a side rule: impure תרומה, which must be burned anyway, may be used as fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה has to be destroyed by burning. The משנה allows it to be burned in a useful way, as fuel for a fire. So the כהן may get benefit from the fire while the תרומה is being destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: One may light a fire or a lamp

phrases.english: And one may ignite a fire with bread and with oil of teruma.
phrases.notes: This is talking about impure תרומה, which may not be eaten but can be used as fuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַדְלִיקִין בְּפַת וּבְשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical detail about the impure תרומה mentioned in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה bread and oil may be used as fuel for a fire.

steps.title: קדשים slaughtered with intent for outside their time or place are burned
steps.stepSummary: Any קדשים slaughtered with the intention to offer or eat them outside their proper time or outside their proper place must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: All קדשים that were slaughtered with intent for outside their time or outside their place must be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list of burned items with sacrifices that were ruined by a wrong intention at the time of slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal itself was fine, but the wrong thought during the slaughter made the קרבן invalid. Even so, it is still קדשים, and disqualified קדשים are destroyed by burning, not by burial.

keyTerms.meaning: Intending to offer or eat the קרבן after its allowed time
Intending to offer or eat the קרבן outside its allowed place
Sacrificial animals

steps.whatToRemember: There are two lists. Some forbidden items are buried (Step 17). Others are burned: חמץ, impure תרומה, foods of ערלה and כלאי הכרם, and קדשים ruined by a wrong intention.

phrases.english: All sacrificial animals that were slaughtered
beyond their time or outside their place,
phrases.notes: This means the person slaughtering intended to offer or eat the קרבן at the wrong time or place.

phrases.english: those shall be burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ חוּץ לִזְמַנָּן וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of burned items that began in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים slaughtered with intent for outside their time or place must be burned.
